The '''2011–12 Czech First League''', known as the [[Gambrinus (beer)|Gambrinus]] liga for sponsorship reasons, was the 19th season of the [[Czech Republic]]'s top-tier [[Association football|football]] league. It began on 29 July 2011 and was originally due to end on 26 May 2012,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://fotbal.idnes.cz/dukla-olomouc-0-0-domaci-velkemu-tlaku-po-prestavce-odolali-p3a-/fotbal.aspx?c=A110729_172327_fotbal_min |title=Dukla – Olomouc 0:0, domácí velkému tlaku po přestávce odolali |language=cs|newspaper=Mladá fronta Dnes|publisher=Mafra|date=29 July 2011 |access-date=29 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121002092158/http://fotbal.idnes.cz/dukla-olomouc-0-0-domaci-velkemu-tlaku-po-prestavce-odolali-p3a-/fotbal.aspx?c=A110729_172327_fotbal_min |archive-date=2 October 2012 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Fotbalová liga už zná program, derby Sparta – Slavia se hraje v září|url=http://fotbal.idnes.cz/fotbalova-liga-uz-zna-program-derby-sparta-slavia-se-hraje-v-zari-px5-/fotbal.asp?c=A110624_113648_fotbal_mn|newspaper=Mladá fronta Dnes|publisher=Mafra|date=24 June 2011|access-date=25 June 2011|language=cs}}</ref> although due to the [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic]]'s qualification for the [[UEFA Euro 2012]], the end of the season was brought forward to 12 May 2012.<ref>{{cite news|first=Miloslav|last=Novák|url=http://fotbal.idnes.cz/fotbalove-terminy-v-roce-2012-na-jare-se-v-cesku-hraje-dvakrat-tydne-phj-/fotbal.aspx?c=A120102_182253_fotbal_min|title=Fotbalové termíny v roce 2012: na jaře se v Česku hraje dvakrát týdně|language=cs|newspaper=Mladá fronta Dnes|publisher=Mafra|date=3 January 2012|access-date=8 May 2012}}</ref> [[FC Viktoria Plzeň|Viktoria Plzeň]] were the defending champions, having won their first Czech Republic championship [[2010–11 Czech First League|the previous season]].

[[AC Sparta Prague|Sparta Prague]] started the season with eight consecutive wins, the first such occurrence in league history.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sparta – Slavia 3:0, osmý duel, osmá výhra, rival vzdoroval jen chvíli|language=cs|url=http://fotbal.idnes.cz/sparta-slavia-3-0-osmy-duel-osma-vyhra-rival-vzdoroval-jen-chvili-pw8-/fotbal.aspx?c=A110926_183342_fotbal_pes|newspaper=Mladá fronta Dnes|publisher=Mafra|date=26 September 2011 |access-date=26 September 2011}}</ref> Sparta broke their own record when they won their ninth straight league match and opened up a 10-point lead at the top of the table.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://fotbal.idnes.cz/sparta-vylepsila-svuj-rekord-na-druhe-bohemians-ma-naskok-deset-bodu-1ii-/fotbal.aspx?c=A111001_150242_fotbal_vl |title=Sparta vylepšila svůj rekord, na druhé Bohemians má náskok deset bodů |language=cs |newspaper=Mladá fronta Dnes|publisher=Mafra|date=1 October 2011 |access-date=28 January 2012}}</ref>

The title was decided on the last day of the season, with [[FC Slovan Liberec|Liberec]] hosting [[FC Viktoria Plzeň|Viktoria Plzeň]] in the knowledge that a win for either team would seal the title, with a draw being enough for Liberec to retain first place.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://plzensky.denik.cz/fotbal_region/liberec-vs-plzen-bitva-o-titul-slibuje-drama-20120511.html|title=Liberec vs. Plzeň. Bitva o titul slibuje drama|language=cs|newspaper=[[Deník]]|publisher=[[Vltava Labe Media]]|date=12 May 2012 |access-date=4 August 2019}}</ref> In front of a sold-out stadium at [[Stadion u Nisy]], Liberec held the visitors to a goalless draw, winning the league for the third time since 2002.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://sport.aktualne.cz/fotbal/liberec-udrzel-proti-plzni-remizu-a-slavi-titul/r~i:article:744583/|title=Liberec udržel proti Plzni remízu a slaví titul|website=Aktuálně.cz|publisher=[[Economia]]|date=12 May 2012 |access-date=4 August 2019}}</ref>

==Teams==
[[FK Ústí nad Labem|Ústí nad Labem]] and [[FC Zbrojovka Brno|Zbrojovka Brno]] were relegated to the 2011–12 [[Czech 2. Liga]] after finishing last and second to last, respectively, in the [[2010–11 Czech First League|2010–11 season]]. Ústi nad Labem therefore immediately returned to the second tier, while Brno completed a nineteen-year tenure in the top flight.

The relegated terms were replaced by [[2010–11 Czech 2. Liga|2010–11 2. Liga]] champions [[FK Dukla Prague|Dukla Prague]] and [[FK Viktoria Žižkov|Viktoria Žižkov]]. Viktoria Žižkov returned after a two-year absence, while Dukla Prague made their debut in the league; however, the Dukla Prague name returned to the league after seventeen seasons, with a [[Dukla Prague|club of the same name]] having played in the top Czech football division until then. The newly promoted clubs were granted licenses to play top-division football on 13 June 2011.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://fotbal.idnes.cz/fotbalovi-prvoligovi-novacci-dukla-a-zizkov-maji-profesionalni-licenci-1an-/fotbal.asp?c=A110613_180946_fotbal_mn |title=Fotbaloví prvoligoví nováčci Dukla a Žižkov mají profesionální licenci |language=cs |newspaper=Mladá fronta Dnes|publisher=Mafra|date=13 June 2011 |access-date= 14 June 2011}}</ref>

Viktoria Žižkov became the first team to be relegated on 5 May 2012 after [[FC Baník Ostrava|Ostrava]] beat [[1. FK Příbram|Příbram]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://fotbal.idnes.cz/utkani-28-kola-prvni-fotbalove-ligy-pribram-ostrava-f8z-/fotbal.aspx?c=A120504_165644_fotbal_min|title=Příbram – Ostrava 1:2, výhra hostů poslala do druhé ligy Žižkov |language=cs |newspaper=Mladá fronta Dnes|publisher=Mafra|date=5 May 2012|access-date=5 May 2012}}</ref>
